Thank you all for flagging these critical issues. This is exactly why we needed to pause before closing. Let me address each point and make decisions on ownership.

First, Mateo -- please go ahead and attach those deployment audit records to the incident immediately. We need full visibility into which production jobs used the exposed credential, and those records must be preserved immutably for the 400-day retention period Hana identified. Hana, please update the incident checklist to reflect that retention requirement so it's documented.

Second, Leah -- the 24-hour contractual notification window is our most urgent concern. The credential was exposed during yesterday's release, so we need to determine the exact timestamp of exposure and calculate whether we're approaching or already past that window. Please share the list of the three regulated customers and their specific contractual clauses to the incident channel now. Regarding ownership of the notification process -- I'll take responsibility for ensuring the notices are sent and tracked. I'll coordinate with whoever owns each customer relationship to get the notices out as quickly as possible once we have the full list and confirm which deployment jobs touched those customers' environments.

Third, I'm recommending we extend this incident review past 4 PM today. We cannot responsibly close until we've confirmed: (1) the deployment audit records are attached and preserved immutably, (2) the customer notification obligation is assessed and underway, and (3) we have a complete picture of which production jobs used the exposed credential.

Does anyone have concerns with this plan, or is there anything else we need to address before we proceed?
